newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on auction result, peso.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on auction result, peso.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed off sessions highs, but was still up 35 basis points at 22.25 percent in response to nervousness triggered by greater-then-expected rises in primary rates the night before and a weak peso, traders said.
"The money market's fortunes have been closely linked to the forex market of late, almost as if it were the same market, and that hit us today," a trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended 1.7 centavos softer at 7.9290/7.9310 per dollar.

Bellwether 27-day Cetes gained 127 basis points to 21.86 percent at Banco de Mexico's Tuesday evening primary auction, compared with an increase of 63 basis points forecast in a prior Reuters survey of money market traders.
Dealers said overnight rates on Cetes ended below a peak of 23.30 percent due to a big player who tried to lower rates.
"Someone was long on low-cost paper and tried to turn the market around," another dealer said.
Traders said rates were also under upside pressure from tight market liquidity.

The central bank drained a hefty 6.449 billion pesos from the secondary market through six auctions, which it assigned at rates of between 24.54-25.34 percent, and maturities of between one and 15 days.
Overnight rates on bank paper, meanwhile, closed up 65 basis points at a session high of 24.55 percent.
Liquidity of 2.224 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation.
